title: Mormon Teaches in the Synagogue
summary: Mormon speaks to the people in the synagogue they built as a place of worship.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon taught the people in a synagogue they had built for worship.
Moroni writes words of his father Mormon concerning faith, hope, and charity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon is visible addressing people gathered in the synagogue.
unspecified_visual_details: The synagogue's architecture and furnishings.
The people's appearance and number.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse frames the following teaching as Mormon's words, recorded by Moroni.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni as present in the synagogue; his writing is a framing statement.

title: Mormon Addresses the Brethren
summary: Mormon addresses the brethren, identifying them as followers of Christ and judging them by their peaceable conduct.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon addresses his beloved brethren and says he is permitted to speak by God's grace and calling.
He describes his audience as peaceable followers of Christ with hope of entering the Lord's rest.
He judges them by their peaceable walk with people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon continues speaking to the gathered brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The brethren's individual identities and appearances.
Any specific gestures or arrangement of the gathering.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is continuous teaching, not a separate enacted event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God or Jesus Christ visibly; their mention does not describe an appearance.

title: Works and Intent
summary: Mormon teaches that works reveal character and that gifts or prayers without real intent do not profit the giver.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon cites the teaching that people are known by their works.
He teaches that an evil person cannot do good, and that a gift or prayer without real intent profits nothing.
Such conduct is not counted as righteousness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon speaks to the brethren; no specific example is narrated as an event.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether any listener is giving a gift or praying.
The appearance or setting details beyond the synagogue.

narration.text: by their works ye shall know them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The teaching about gifts and prayer is general, not a narrated demonstration.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a gift-giving or prayer event as occurring in the synagogue.

title: Gifts and Prayer Without Sincerity
summary: Mormon teaches that a grudging gift or prayer without real intent is counted as evil and profits nothing.

explicit_facts.text: An evil person who gives grudgingly is counted as retaining the gift and is counted evil before God.
Prayer without real intent of heart profits nothing, and God receives no such prayer.
An evil person cannot do good or give a good gift.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon continues his teaching to the brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: Any specific gift or prayer being performed.
The listeners' reactions.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are general principles, not a specific event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a named or identifiable giver, recipient, or prayer.

title: Good and Evil
summary: Mormon teaches that good comes from God and evil from the devil, contrasting their invitations.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon compares a bitter fountain that cannot bring forth good water with a good fountain that cannot bring forth bitter water.
He teaches that good comes from God and evil from the devil, who continually invites and entices to sin.
That which is of God invites and entices people to do good, love God, and serve him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fountain language may be conveyed as a teaching metaphor rather than a literal scene.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal fountain, devil, or divine figure.

narration.text: all things which are good cometh of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fountain is a figure of speech; the verses do not narrate a visible fountain or the devil appearing.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal supernatural confrontation or a visible devil.

title: Judge Good from Evil
summary: Mormon teaches the brethren to judge good and evil by what invites people toward Christ and goodness or away from them.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon warns against judging evil to be of God or good to be of the devil.
He says people can know good from evil as plainly as daylight from dark night.
The Spirit of Christ is given to every person to know good from evil; that which invites to good and belief in Christ is of God.
That which persuades people to do evil, disbelieve in Christ, deny him, and not serve God is of the devil.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon speaks continuously; the daylight and dark-night comparison can remain verbal rather than depicted literally.
unspecified_visual_details: Any person or force embodying good or evil.

narration.text: as plain, that ye may know with a perfect knowledge

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The daylight comparison is a teaching figure, not an enacted transition from day to night.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Spirit of Christ, devil, or angels appearing; no appearance is described here.

title: Search in the Light of Christ
summary: Mormon warns against wrongful judgment, urges diligent search for good, and introduces his teaching on faith.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon warns that people will be judged with the same judgment they use.
He urges the brethren to search diligently in the light of Christ, lay hold upon every good thing, and not condemn it.
He asks how they can lay hold upon every good thing.
He announces that he will explain faith as the way to lay hold upon every good thing.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visible manifestation of the light of Christ.

narration.text: search diligently in the light of Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The light of Christ is described as a principle for judgment, not as a visible light effect.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural beam, figure, or other physical manifestation of the light.

title: Angels and the Coming of Christ
summary: Mormon teaches that God sent angels to minister and make known Christ's coming, and declared through prophets that Christ would come.

explicit_facts.text: God sent angels to minister to the children of men and make manifest the coming of Christ.
God declared to prophets that Christ would come.
God manifested good things to people in diverse ways; all good things come of Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be shown as Mormon speaking, without staging past angelic or prophetic events.
unspecified_visual_details: The angels' appearance, the prophets' identities, and any specific manifestations.

narration.text: he sent angels to minister unto the children of men

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses summarize past divine acts; they do not establish a particular angel or prophet as visibly present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a historical scene, named prophet, or angelic appearance.

title: Faith Before Christ's Coming
summary: Mormon teaches that through angels' ministry and God's word, people exercised faith in Christ and laid hold upon good things until Christ came.

explicit_facts.text: By angelic ministry and God's word, people began to exercise faith in Christ and lay hold upon every good thing until Christ's coming.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon continues teaching; the earlier people and angels need not be shown as present.
unspecified_visual_details: The people referred to, their location, and any particular angelic ministry.

narration.text: men began to exercise faith in Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a summary of events before Christ's coming, not a present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unspecified group or angel in a fabricated historical episode.

title: Faith in Christ's Name
summary: Mormon teaches that after Christ came, people were saved by faith in his name and quotes Christ's promise about asking the Father in faith for what is good.

explicit_facts.text: After Christ came, people were saved by faith in his name and became sons of God.
Christ spoke to the fathers, promising that what they ask the Father in his name, if good and asked in faith, would be done unto them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon remains the visible speaker; Christ's words are quoted as reported speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The fathers addressed by Christ and the circumstances in which he spoke.

narration.text: Whatsoever thing ye shall ask the Father in my name, which is good

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports Christ's words; it does not depict Christ physically present in the synagogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Christ speaking to unnamed fathers as a new scene.

title: Christ in the Heavens
summary: Mormon asks whether miracles have ceased because Christ ascended and sat at God's right hand, and teaches that Christ advocates for the faithful.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon refers to Christ ascending into heaven and sitting at the right hand of God to claim mercy for people.
Christ answered the ends of the law, claims those who have faith in him, advocates for people, and dwells eternally in the heavens.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The ascension and heavenly advocacy are reported teaching, not a present event in the synagogue.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of God and Christ in heaven.

narration.text: have miracles ceased because Christ hath ascended into heaven

doctrinal_or_story_notes: No visual description of Christ or God is supplied in these verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a new heavenly scene or invent appearances.

title: Angels Continue to Minister
summary: Mormon says miracles and angelic ministry have not ceased; angels minister according to Christ's command and show themselves to people of strong faith.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon declares that miracles and angels ministering to people have not ceased.
Angels are subject to Christ's command and show themselves to people of strong faith and a firm mind in godliness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be presented as Mormon speaking without showing an angel, since no particular appearance is narrated.
unspecified_visual_details: The angels' forms, the people to whom they show themselves, and the setting of any such appearance.

narration.text: neither have angels ceased to minister unto the children of men

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a general assertion and description of ministry, not a specific angelic encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not create an angelic appearance or name an otherwise unspecified recipient.

title: The Work of Angels
summary: Mormon describes angels calling people to repentance and declaring Christ's word to chosen servants, preparing others to have faith and receive the Holy Ghost.

explicit_facts.text: Angels call people to repentance, fulfill the Father's covenants, prepare the way, and declare Christ's word to chosen vessels who testify of him.
Through this, the Lord prepares others to have faith in Christ and for the Holy Ghost to have place in their hearts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon can be shown teaching; these general ministries need not be staged as a specific encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angels, chosen vessels, recipients, and location of any ministry.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe the office and purpose of angelic ministry without narrating a particular event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named angels, chosen vessels, or scenes of testimony.

title: Christ's Invitation and Promise
summary: Mormon quotes Christ's teachings on faith, repentance, baptism, and salvation.

explicit_facts.text: Christ said that faith in him gives power to do what is expedient in him.
Christ called people everywhere to repent, come to him, be baptized in his name, and have faith in him to be saved.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon is the visible speaker while quoting Christ's teachings.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience of Christ's original statements and any baptismal setting.

narration.text: Repent all ye ends of the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are reported teachings, not a present appearance of Christ.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a baptism or Christ physically speaking in this scene.

title: Have Miracles Ceased?
summary: Mormon asks whether miracles, angelic appearances, and the power of the Holy Ghost have ceased, then answers that miracles and angelic ministry come by faith.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon asks whether God will show the truth with power and glory at the last day and whether the day of miracles has ceased.
He asks whether angels have ceased to appear and whether the Holy Ghost's power has been withheld while people remain to be saved.
He answers no: miracles are wrought by faith, and angels appear and minister by faith; cessation would be because of unbelief.
Mormon says salvation requires faith in Christ's name, and without faith people would be as though there had been no redemption.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon speaks through a sequence of questions and answers.
unspecified_visual_details: Any miracle, angelic appearance, or manifestation of the Holy Ghost.

narration.text: Behold I say unto you, Nay

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The questions and general claims do not narrate a specific miracle or appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage miracles, angels, or the Holy Ghost as visible events.

title: Mormon's Hope for the Brethren
summary: Mormon says he judges better things of the brethren and judges that they have faith in Christ because of their meekness.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon judges that the brethren have faith in Christ because of their meekness.
He says those without faith in Christ are not fit to be numbered among the people of his church.

unspecified_visual_details: Individual expressions or actions that would demonstrate meekness.

narration.text: I judge that ye have faith in Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mormon's judgment is part of his address, not a separately depicted assessment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a named or singled-out listener.

title: Hope through Christ
summary: Mormon turns to hope, teaching that hope comes through Christ's atonement and resurrection, accompanies faith, and requires meekness and lowliness of heart.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon introduces his teaching concerning hope and asks how faith can be attained without hope.
He teaches that hope through Christ's atonement and resurrection is to be raised to eternal life, according to the promise.
A person with faith must have hope; without faith there is no hope.
Faith and hope require meekness and lowliness of heart.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon continues his address without any enacted resurrection scene.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visual representation of atonement, resurrection, or eternal life.

narration.text: ye shall have hope through the atonement of Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The resurrection is taught as a future hope, not depicted as an event occurring here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray Christ's atonement or resurrection as a present scene.

title: Meekness and Charity
summary: Mormon teaches that meekness, confession that Jesus is the Christ, and charity belong together; he describes charity and calls it the pure love of Christ.

explicit_facts.text: The meek and lowly in heart are acceptable before God; one who confesses by the Holy Ghost that Jesus is the Christ must have charity.
Mormon describes charity as long-suffering, kind, unenvying, humble, and enduring, among other qualities.
Without charity people are nothing; charity never fails and is the greatest of all.
Charity is the pure love of Christ and endures forever; it will be well with whoever possesses it at the last day.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon remains the speaker; charity's personified grammatical form is not a literal person.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal visual embodiment of charity or the last day.

narration.text: charity is the pure love of Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The description of charity is teaching, not a visible character or enacted series of behaviors.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict charity as a person or stage an unspecified last-day event.

title: Prayer for Charity
summary: Mormon urges the brethren to pray to be filled with Christ's love, become sons of God, and have hope of being purified and like Christ when he appears.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon urges prayer to the Father for the love bestowed on true followers of Jesus Christ.
He says this love may help them become sons of God and have hope of being purified and like Christ when Christ appears.
The chapter's address ends with “Amen.”

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon delivers the closing exhortation to the brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible appearance of Christ, the Father, or purification.

narration.text: pray unto the Father with all the energy of heart

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Christ's appearance is anticipated, not narrated as occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ appearing or the brethren performing a specific prayer gesture.
